findings.title: A byte-for-byte copy of TCB files exempts a user package from admission
findings.resolution: Trust is now (import path, file name, digest): sgoadmit.Trusted(pkgpath, files) requires a TCB package path and each file's manifest entry (shared tcbFileOK with CheckTCB); the content-only digest set is no longer generated. The importer refuses a 'tcb' identity on a non-TCB path (SGO_E_FOREIGN_OBJECT), and so does the linker (sgoIdentConfigErr, generated sgotcb.go list). policy.md reworded. SGO-TCB-002 clause wording ('a function of file digests') is deferred to the version change of SR2, since it is normative text.
findings.regression_test: test-tcb.py copy cases (subset copy of internal/stringslite, whole internal/godebugs, direct compile; digest asserted first); host-lane TestTrusted and TestSGoIdentConfigErr; mutation (content-only Trusted) caught by test-tcb via the importer check
findings.verified_by: reviewer at f71e01af75 (linux/amd64): probes p1/p2 rejected, direct compile rejected, test-tcb ok, conformance 336/336

findings.title: S-Go programs honour GODEBUG, GOTRACEBACK, GOGC, GOMEMLIMIT and GOMAXPROCS
findings.resolution: The S-Go linker marks every binary it links (addstrdata1 runtime.sgoLinked=1, before schedinit). In such a binary gogetenv returns "" for every key (GODEBUG, GOTRACEBACK, GOGC, GOMEMLIMIT, GOMAXPROCS, GOROOT) and getGodebugEarly returns only the build's godebugDefault, so cpuinit and the debug variables use fixed defaults. Upstream-linked binaries (runtime lane) are unchanged. GOMAXPROCS is ignored too (D84, user decision); D82's rationale corrected.
findings.regression_test: conformance proc-env-ignored (panic record exact under GODEBUG=schedtrace,inittrace,gctrace,invalidptr=0,sbrk=1; GOGC=1; GOMEMLIMIT=1; GOTRACEBACK=crash; GOMAXPROCS=1) and proc-env-ignored-ok (stderr exactly empty); mutant without the linker marker fails both (schedtrace/inittrace output); runtime lane TestSGoEnvUpstreamLinked
findings.verified_by: reviewer at bc8027270a (linux/amd64): p4 under hostile env prints only the record; proc-hello with inittrace/gctrace stderr empty; gogetenv sites audited; conformance 341/341; runtime lane ok. Reviewer request: note next to the linker marker that it relies on 'this linker links only S-Go programs', enforced by R3's required -buildid and sgoCheckIdentity.

findings.title: Shipped compile and link accept the whole upstream flag table for S-Go code
findings.resolution: Refuse-by-default allowlists in the shipped tools. compile (base/sgoflags.go, called in noder.LoadPackage once sgoMode is known): S-Go packages accept -o -p -importcfg -pack -complete -trimpath -sgolab -sgocheck -sgotestmain and -m (diagnostic output only); TCB packages accept the driver's TCB command line (-o -p -importcfg -pack -complete -trimpath -std -lang -symabis -asmhdr) with -lang pinned to go1.<goversion>; GOCOMPILEDEBUG, a non-empty GOEXPERIMENT or an experiment set differing from the default, and GOAMD64 != v1 / GOARM64 != v8.0 are refused. link (sgoCheckConfig + sgoidcfg.go): only -o -importcfg -buildmode -buildid -sgodrainbudget -sgogrants -sgoiogrants -sgolab -sgotest; -buildid is required, must be S-Go metadata, and must agree with the link (config lab/test/lab-test, drain, grants) and with the linked packages' spec version and admission digest. The existing named refusals (-X, -checklinkname=0, -linkmode, build modes) keep their messages. Flags upstream already rejects on a platform (-spectre, -asan, -msan on darwin) stay refused by upstream.
findings.regression_test: test-flags.py: 18 compile flags and 3 compiler settings refused with SGO_E_USAGE and no output file; admitted command lines still give the S-Go denials; 13 named link refusals plus -f -s -w -strictdups=0 -randlayout=1 -k=x -installsuffix=x -debugnosplit -race -msan -asan -R; missing/foreign/inconsistent -buildid (lab claiming production, drain, grants) refused; harness self-test that an admitted link is not reported as refused. Host lane TestSGoLinkFlagsAndBuildID (13 build-ID rows). test-identity and test-x10 link with a driver-format -buildid (sgotool.py); test-x10 checks -l is refused instead of comparing a -l build.
findings.verified_by: reviewer at 098959aa24 (linux/amd64): p6 matrix re-run; 19 compile flags and 3 settings refused; link flags, missing/inconsistent -buildid refused; lanes ok; conformance 342/342. Residuals folded into D-R3: link-side GOEXPERIMENT check and GOFIPS140 classification; -goversion refused only by upstream's check, should be SGO_E_USAGE.

findings.title: Dir.Open/Create on a FIFO wedges the program; the drain budget never fires
findings.resolution: (1) Dir.Open/Create open the last component with O_NONBLOCK, fstat it, close and report NotRegularFile (no effect) for anything but a regular file (IsDirectory kept for directories), and clear O_NONBLOCK on success; ENXIO maps to NotRegularFile. (2) Every file system call that can block goes through entersyscall/exitsyscall: linux sgoSys (openat, fstatat, mkdirat, unlinkat, getdents64, ftruncate, and the socket calls), darwin sgoOpenat/Fstatat/Fstat/Mkdirat/Unlinkat/Ftruncate, darwin readdir through syscall_syscalln with heap buffers. No caller holds a runtime lock. D55 unchanged: file calls are still not cancellation points. The NotRegularFile kind and the regular-files-only rule join SPEC-FILE in the 0.7.0 change (doc item D-R4).
findings.regression_test: conformance file-open-fifo (runner mkfifo; Open and Create -> NotRegularFile with NoEffect, under a 5 s watchdog); runtime lane TestSGoBlockedOpenDoesNotStallGC (blocking openat on a FIFO through a test hook while 20 GCs run; the mutant without entersyscall hangs until the 60 s test timeout); linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 vet of the runtime
findings.verified_by: reviewer at 426276e16c (linux/amd64): p7 FIFO probe returns NotRegularFile at once; TestSGoBlockedOpenDoesNotStallGC passes; linux mutant without entersyscall in sgoSys hangs (test killed after 2m); race lane TestSGo ok; conformance 342/342

findings.title: A captured named result is reassigned by return <operands>
findings.resolution: sgoAssignments treats a return with operands as assigning every named result of its innermost enclosing function (FuncDecl or FuncLit, tracked with a stack during Inspect) and reports SGO_E_CAPTURE_NOT_FINAL at the return when one is captured. A bare return still assigns nothing. ctl-defer-assigns-named-result now also expects the diagnostic at 'return 1, 2', which is correct per SGO-MEM-002 (the deferred literal captures b and the return assigns it). Recording the implicit-assignment forms in SGO-MEM-002 compile_link_checks is normative text, deferred to the SR2 version change (doc item D-R5).
findings.regression_test: conformance mem-capture-named-result-return (FuncDecl), mem-capture-named-result-return-literal (FuncLit), mem-capture-named-result-bare-return (run, exit 0); ctl-return-operands-nursery unchanged
findings.verified_by: reviewer at f35be2e975 (linux/amd64): probes p8, p9 rejected; p10a (multi-value return, only b captured) rejected once naming b; p10b (nested literal return) not flagged; conformance 339/339; test-check 323; second diagnostic in ctl-defer-assigns-named-result agreed as correct

findings.title: File confinement: Create truncates before the chain check; Mkdir/Remove act on a parent descriptor after verifying it (TOCTOU)
findings.resolution: linux: sgoResolve first tries one openat2(root, path, RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS) (syscall 437); EAGAIN/EINTR retry up to sgoResolveRetries then PathRejected; EXDEV/ELOOP -> PathRejected; ENOSYS (kernel < 5.6) falls back to the component walk for the rest of the run. Create truncates only after resolution (R4 commit). Mkdir/Remove re-resolve the parent after the effect and compare (dev, ino); if the parent left the grant they return the new kind PathRaced with NoEffect false (D56: the effect is reported). darwin and pre-5.6 linux keep the walk: the residual (a file may be created outside the grant through a raced path, never truncated) goes into SPEC-FILE 0.7.0 (D-R6).
findings.regression_test: runtime lane TestSGoRenameRaces with a test hook (sgoIORaceHook, sites 'walk' and 'effect'): Remove and Mkdir with the parent moved out -> PathRaced, NoEffect false; Create through a raced walk -> the outside file keeps its content and the result is NotFound/PathRejected. Mutants: without the post-effect check both PathRaced rows fail; with O_TRUNC restored the outside file is truncated and the test fails. linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 vet; openat2 itself needs a linux run (reviewer).
findings.note: Partly addressed by R4's change: Create now opens without O_TRUNC and truncates only after the chain verification succeeded, so a file reached through a raced path is never truncated (it may still be created). openat2 and Mkdir/Remove re-verification remain.

reopen.regression: openat2 path: EINVAL for a mode without O_CREAT made every Open/ReadFile an IOError (7 conformance cases failed); O_DIRECTORY on a trailing symlink gave ENOTDIR -> NotFound instead of PathRejected (TestSGoDirList)
reopen.fix: sgoOpenBeneath drops mode without O_CREAT; strips O_DIRECTORY and checks S_IFDIR with fstat after the open (ENOTDIR otherwise); falls back to the walk on ENOSYS and EPERM (seccomp); sgoNoOpenat2 is an atomic.Bool
reopen.regression_test: TestSGoResolutionPathsAgree: 14 file-confined-paths outcomes through openat2 and through the forced walk (SGoForceWalk); runs on every target (darwin: walk only)
reopen.process: linux-sensitive fixes go to re-check only after the linux CI legs are green

findings.title: Running build scripts dirties tracked evidence files
findings.regression_test: CI clean-tree steps; locally build-stage0 + checks leave sgo/evidence unchanged
findings.fix: scripts write tracked evidence only with SGO_RECORD=1; otherwise to $SGO_OUT/evidence (default $SGO_CACHE/out); CI uploads from $SGO_OUT and every sgo-w00/sgo-spec/sgo-runtime job ends with a clean-tree check (git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)

findings.title: Driver reuses cached TCB archives on a 'complete' marker alone; SGO_CACHE unclassified
findings.regression_test: test-tcb: one flipped byte in the cached runtime.a is rebuilt byte for byte; mutant (manifest presence only) fails
findings.fix: a TCB cache entry ends with manifest.sha256 (sha256 of each archive); an entry is reused only if it lists exactly the expected archives and each matches, otherwise it is removed and rebuilt. SGO_CACHE and TMPDIR classification goes to the D77 audit
findings.scope: integrity against corruption, stale and partial entries; not tamper-proof against a writer of $SGO_CACHE (who can also replace the tool binaries). Tamper resistance would need archive digests recorded outside the cache (optional).

findings.title: Allocation under c.lock in sgoChanReserve
findings.resolution: sgoChanReserve allocates the permit once before lock(&c.lock) and reuses it across retries (the task's scope cannot change while it is blocked); the order of c.reserved++ and sgoPermitLink is unchanged. The audit of the other allocation sites under runtime locks (sgo_native_ops.go, sgo_ready.go) and the static check script are still open.
findings.regression_test: sgo/scripts/lock-alloc-check.py in sgo-spec CI; mutation: it reports all 9 sites in the pre-fix sources
findings.fix: no allocation under an S-Go runtime lock: sgoChanReserve (d329fa71b7); native send/recv, Event.Wait and limiter Acquire allocate the wait record with the lock released and retry; blocking select allocates sel/ws/park records before sgoSelLock

residual.finding: append to c.queue under c.lock (sgoChanCommit, sgoNativeTrySend, sgoNativeTryRecv refill); queue[1:] dropped capacity so steady-state buffered channels reallocated under the lock
residual.fix: fixed ring allocated at channel creation (buf, head, count; qpush/qpop clear popped slots); netfake backlog drained one pop per lock hold; lock-alloc-check also reports append( and checks functions documented as running under the caller's lock
residual.regression_test: TestSGoChanRingStable (10 000 pairs: FIFO, ring identity, cleared slots; mutant without the slot clear fails); lock-alloc-check reports the 3 queue sites on the pre-fix sources

findings.finding: EPERM from a real openat2 (immutable or append-only file) switched resolution to the walk for the rest of the process
findings.fix: availability decided once by sgoOpenat2Probe (openat2(dirfd, ".", O_PATH, RESOLVE_BENEATH)); an open's EPERM maps through sgoErrKind
findings.regression_test: TestSGoOpenat2EPERMIsAnOpenError (fault hook SGoOpenat2FaultOnce, openat2 open counter); linux only, skipped without openat2

findings.finding: runtime-design §5 said a channel lock is never held while taking another; native select holds every arm's lock
findings.fix: §5 states the order: none, one, or one select's arm set in ascending address order (sgoSelLock, the only multi-lock site), then sgoSleepLock

findings.finding: walk-mode Create raced by a rename could create a file outside the grant and report PathRejected (NoEffect true): an unreported effect (D56, §12.3)
findings.fix: the walk creates exclusively first (O_EXCL), then opens without O_CREAT on EEXIST; a failed verification after this walk created the file returns PathRaced (NoEffect false), not undone; SGO-FILE-002 v3
findings.regression_test: TestSGoCreateRaceReported (forced walk): created -> PathRaced with an empty file outside; existing -> unchanged, NoEffect true; mutant (created never set) fails

self_findings.claim: Matrix status fields record what ran
self_findings.finding: 17 cases (I01-I07, T01-T06, T08, S01, S15, S19) had executed '<WP>: passed' evidence from their last required work package (W09/W10) but still had implementation_status pending / execution_status unrun. The W09 and W10 closures appended evidence without flipping the status fields.
self_findings.resolution: Flipped only cases whose last required work package has a '<WP>: passed' evidence entry (checked by the script that made the change). T07 stays pending (PARTIAL, D82). guarantee-check.py (D76) will fail on the inconsistency in either direction.

self_findings.claim: Q04: every accepted feature is explicit in the closed registry
self_findings.finding: The registry still carries its 0.1.0 text ('No row is admitted') and every implemented family is 'specified_not_admitted' with empty admitted_in and evidence, although W03-W10 implemented, enforced and tested them. The registry understates what the toolchain accepts. Row status is part of the admission digest, so correcting it moves every identity.

self_findings.claim: Each frozen clause records where it is implemented and what ran
self_findings.finding: 62 frozen clauses still said 'none yet' in their progress fields although implemented and tested in W02-W10. These fields are excluded from clause digests, so the text was stale but no identity was wrong.
self_findings.resolution: sgo/scripts/fill-progress.py filled the fields from the work packages already named, the family's implementation files, the clause's own fixtures, and the work-package evidence READMEs. No digest changed (spec-tool update leaves SGO_SPEC_ADMISSION.json untouched). guarantee-check.py fails if any frozen clause says 'none yet'.

self_findings.location: 76 added files: sgo/model, sgo/scripts, sgo/bench, sgo/examples
self_findings.claim: Every file added by S-Go carries the S-Go BSD header (D81)
self_findings.finding: 76 added source files (model, scripts, benchmarks, and the shipped examples) had no license header. LICENSE/PATENTS and vendored code were unchanged, no foreign license or copyright marker was found, and no upstream header was removed.
self_findings.resolution: license-audit.py --fix inserted the header (after any #! line). Model tests, test-fmt (354 files) and test-examples (pipeline, service, replay) pass afterwards. No TCB file changed. license-audit.py runs in sgo-spec CI.
self_findings.regression_test: license-audit.py (mutation: LICENSE edit, SPDX marker, missing header all caught)
